claim: Cerebellar granule cells constitute the majority of neurons in the brain.
source_text: Cerebellar granule cells constitute the majority of neurons in the brain and are the primary conveyors of sensory and motor-related mossy fiber information to Purkinje cells.
evidence_reasoning: This statement is presented as established fact and is supported by citations in the introduction (De Schutter and Bjaalie, 2001; Herculano-Houzel and Lent, 2005; Watson et al., 2012) indicating it draws from prior literature.

claim: Granule cells are the primary conveyors of sensory and motor-related mossy fiber information to Purkinje cells.
source_text: Cerebellar granule cells constitute the majority of neurons in the brain and are the primary conveyors of sensory and motor-related mossy fiber information to Purkinje cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as established knowledge about cerebellar circuitry, supported by the broader literature on cerebellar anatomy.

claim: Individual granule cells receive mossy fiber inputs from multiple precerebellar nuclei.
source_text: The functional capability of the cerebellum hinges on whether individual granule cells receive mossy fiber inputs from multiple precerebellar nuclei or are instead unimodal; this distinction is unresolved.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly tested and supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript showing convergence of ECN and BPN inputs onto individual granule cells.

claim: Separate sensory (upper body proprioceptive) and basilar pontine pathways converge onto individual granule cells.
source_text: Using cell-type-specific projection mapping with synaptic resolution, we observed the convergence of separate sensory (upper body proprioceptive) and basilar pontine pathways onto individual granule cells and mapped this convergence across cerebellar cortex.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding of the study supported by direct experimental observations using viral tracing and confocal microscopy.

claim: The convergence of sensory and pontine pathways has a reproducible, region-specific cerebellar topography.
source_text: Using cell-type-specific projection mapping with synaptic resolution, we observed the convergence of separate sensory (upper body proprioceptive) and basilar pontine pathways onto individual granule cells and mapped this convergence across cerebellar cortex.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the systematic mapping data presented in Figures 3-5 showing regional variation in convergence patterns.

claim: The convergent basilar pontine pathways carry corollary discharges from upper body motor cortical areas.
source_text: We also provide evidence that the convergent basilar pontine pathways carry corollary discharges from upper body motor cortical areas.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the retrograde tracing data showing M1 inputs to BPN neurons projecting to the paramedian lobule, combined with inference about the functional nature of these signals.

claim: Merging of corollary and sensory streams is a critical component of circuit models of predictive motor control.
source_text: Such merging of related corollary and sensory streams is a critical component of circuit models of predictive motor control.
evidence_reasoning: This statement draws on established theoretical models of motor control cited in the manuscript.

claim: The cerebellum is critical for coordinating movement and for learning sensorimotor relationships.
source_text: The cerebellum is critical for coordinating movement and for learning sensorimotor relationships (Ito, 2006, 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Granule cells constitute over half the neurons of the mammalian brain.
source_text: Sensory and motor-related afference to the cerebellum is largely conveyed by mossy fiber inputs to granule cells, which notably constitute over half the neurons of the mammalian brain (De Schutter and Bjaalie, 2001; Herculano-Houzel and Lent, 2005; Watson et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This quantitative claim is supported by three citations to prior literature.

claim: Granule cells have on average only four dendrites.
source_text: Granule cells are simple neurons, having on average only four dendrites, each of which receives a single, large, excitatory mossy fiber input (Gray, 1961; Eccles et al., 1967; Palay and Chan-Palay, 1974; Jakab and Hamori, 1988).
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical fact is supported by multiple classical citations.

claim: Each granule cell dendrite receives a single, large, excitatory mossy fiber input.
source_text: Granule cells are simple neurons, having on average only four dendrites, each of which receives a single, large, excitatory mossy fiber input (Gray, 1961; Eccles et al., 1967; Palay and Chan-Palay, 1974; Jakab and Hamori, 1988).
evidence_reasoning: This structural feature is established by classical anatomical studies cited.

claim: Multimodal granule cells enable expansion recoding of cerebellar afference as predicted by Marr-Albus theory.
source_text: Such mixing of mossy fiber inputs was a critical aspect of the expansion recoding of cerebellar afference performed by granule cells in the influential Marr-Albus theory of cerebellar function (Marr, 1969; Blomfield and Marr, 1970; Albus, 1971).
evidence_reasoning: This connects the experimental findings to theoretical predictions from cited classical theories.

claim: Multimodal granule cells were found in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish.
source_text: Electrophysiological evidence was found for multimodal granule cells in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish (Sawtell, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from prior work supported by citation.

claim: Previous mammalian studies failed to positively identify more than one input source converging onto individual cerebellar granule cells.
source_text: Such studies in the mammal have failed to positively identify more than one input source converging onto individual cerebellar granule cells (Jorntell and Ekerot, 2006; Arenz et al., 2008; Bengtsson and Jorntell, 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This summarizes findings from prior electrophysiological studies with citations.

claim: Previous electrophysiological studies did not systematically examine granule cells across cerebellar cortex.
source_text: However, these electrophysiological studies did not systematically examine granule cells across cerebellar cortex, nor did they test the most numerous mossy fiber inputs, those originating from the basilar pontine nucleus (BPN) (Brodal and Bjaalie, 1992).
evidence_reasoning: This is a critical assessment of prior work based on methodological limitations, supported by citation about BPN inputs.

claim: The majority of BPN input originates from output messages of the cerebral cortex, superior colliculus, red nucleus, and other motor centers.
source_text: The majority of BPN input originates from output messages of the cerebral cortex, superior colliculus, red nucleus, and other motor centers (Burne et al., 1981; Mihailoff et al., 1989; Panto et al., 1995; Schwarz and Thier, 1999; Leergaard et al., 2000; Leergaard, 2003; Tziridis et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical fact is supported by multiple citations to prior tracing studies.

claim: BPN mossy fibers are in a position to carry copies of motor commands—corollary discharges—into the cerebellum.
source_text: Therefore BPN mossy fibers are in a position to carry copies of motor commands—corollary discharges—into the cerebellum (Sperry, 1950; von Holst and Mittelstaedt, 1950; Poulet and Hedwig, 2007; Glickstein and Doron, 2008; Sommer and Wurtz, 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the anatomical connectivity, supported by citations on corollary discharge theory.

claim: ECN carries forelimb and upper-trunk proprioceptive information to the cerebellum.
source_text: To test both the multimodal nature of granule cells and their specific role in merging pontine and sensory streams, we examined the intersection of the BPN pathway and a primary sensory precerebellar pathway related to motor output—forelimb and upper-trunk proprioceptive information projecting to the cerebellum through the external cuneate nucleus (ECN) of the hindbrain (Campbell et al., 1974; Akintunde and Eisenman, 1994; Quy et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ECN and BPN inputs synapse onto the same granule cells.
source_text: We found that ECN and BPN inputs synapse onto the same granule cells, with a reproducible, region-specific, cerebellar topography.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding directly supported by the anatomical tracing and microscopy data presented.

claim: ECN and BPN inputs primarily project to mostly non-overlapping regions of the cerebellum at a gross level.
source_text: As has been previously reported, at a gross level the ECN and BPN target mostly non-overlapping regions of the cerebellum (Akintunde and Eisenman, 1994; Serapide et al., 1994, 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by both prior literature and confirmed by the current study's observations.

claim: ECN inputs primarily project to the ipsilateral cerebellar vermis.
source_text: ECN inputs primarily project to the ipsilateral cerebellar vermis and BPN inputs bilaterally terminate in the cerebellar hemispheres (Figure 1C,D).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: BPN inputs bilaterally terminate in the cerebellar hemispheres.
source_text: ECN inputs primarily project to the ipsilateral cerebellar vermis and BPN inputs bilaterally terminate in the cerebellar hemispheres (Figure 1C,D).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: ECN and BPN axons co-terminate in multiple cerebellar areas including the vermis, lateral vermis, simple lobule, paraflocculus, Crus1, Crus2, paramedian lobule, and copula of the pyramis.
source_text: Such areas include the vermis, lateral vermis, simple lobule, paraflocculus, Crus1, Crus2, paramedian lobule, and copula of the pyramis (Figure 1D).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed and documented in the experimental data.

claim: Within co-termination areas, ECN and BPN axons terminate within very close proximity (<50 µm).
source_text: Within these areas, ECN and BPN axons terminate within very close proximity (<50 µm), well within the length of the dendritic arbors of granule cells (Figure 1D, inset).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement from the microscopy data.

claim: The proximity of ECN and BPN terminations is well within the length of the dendritic arbors of granule cells.
source_text: Within these areas, ECN and BPN axons terminate within very close proximity (<50 µm), well within the length of the dendritic arbors of granule cells (Figure 1D, inset).
evidence_reasoning: This combines the measured proximity data with knowledge of granule cell dendritic arbor dimensions.

claim: 40% of proprioceptive granule cells make synapses with both ECN and BPN inputs.
source_text: Based on results from one annotator, 40% of proprioceptive granule cells (2429/5997 in two animals) made obvious synapses (see 'Materials and methods') with both ECN and BPN inputs (Figure 2E).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the systematic annotation of microscopy data.

claim: Subsets of ECN and BPN information streams converge at their first opportunity in the cerebellum—onto granule cells.
source_text: Therefore, subsets of ECN and BPN information streams converge at their first opportunity in the cerebellum—onto granule cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the anatomical data showing direct synaptic convergence.

claim: The paramedian lobule, paraflocculus, and Crus2 are dominated by EB granule cells.
source_text: Lastly, some cerebellar areas are dominated by EB granule cells. These areas include paramedian lobule, the paraflocculus, and Crus2 (Figure 5).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the systematic mapping data presented in Figure 5.

claim: The paramedian lobule, paraflocculus, and Crus2 are 'hotspots' for the intersection of ECN and BPN pathways.
source_text: These areas are 'hotspots' for the intersection of ECN and BPN pathways, where the majority of proprioceptive granule cells also receive BPN inputs.
evidence_reasoning: This characterization is based on the quantitative analysis of granule cell types in these regions.

claim: Differences in the extent and patterns of ECN and BPN convergence suggest that the cerebellum handles proprioceptive information with regional specificity.
source_text: Differences in the extent and patterns of ECN and BPN convergence suggest that the cerebellum handles proprioceptive information with regional specificity.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observed regional variations in convergence patterns.

claim: BPN neurons projecting to the paramedian lobule receive inputs from forelimb/upper body M1 cortical areas.
source_text: For a cerebellar area receiving upper body proprioceptive information, we show that the BPN input receives cortical afferents from an area associated with upper body motor control.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly demonstrated by the combined anterograde and retrograde tracing experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: M1 axons form synapses with BPN neurons projecting to the paramedian lobule.
source_text: Synaptic arrangement between M1 axons and BPNPM. Left, apposition of a M1 axon expressing the presynaptic marker SLC17A7 and a dendrite of a BPNPM in a single confocal slice. Right, apposition of a M1 axon and a SHANK1-containing postsynaptic density of a BPNPM in a single confocal slice.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed using immunohistochemistry for synaptic markers as shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Pontine and proprioceptive streams related to somatotopically similar motor output commands may integrate in multimodal granule cells of the cerebellum.
source_text: Therefore, pontine and proprioceptive streams related to somatotopically similar motor output commands may integrate in multimodal granule cells of the cerebellum.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference combining the convergence data with the M1 input data to suggest functional integration.

claim: Axonal connections carrying pontine information directly converge with proprioceptive pathways onto individual granule cells.
source_text: Our results indicate that axonal connections carrying pontine information directly converge with proprioceptive pathways onto individual granule cells.
evidence_reasoning: This summarizes the primary anatomical finding of the study.

claim: The percentage of proprioceptive granule cells exhibiting convergence with pontine inputs varied across cerebellar areas.
source_text: The percentage of proprioceptive granule cells exhibiting such convergence varied across cerebellar areas.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the regional mapping data in Figures 3-5.

claim: Granule cells receive BPN inputs with the capability of carrying motor cortical corollary discharges.
source_text: In an area exhibiting a high degree of convergence, granule cells receive BPN inputs with the capability of carrying motor cortical corollary discharges.
evidence_reasoning: This combines the anatomical convergence data with the M1-BPN connectivity data to infer functional capability.

claim: The findings establish the multimodal nature of granule cells.
source_text: These findings establish the multimodal nature of granule cells and locate a merging of sensory and corollary pathways in specific cerebellar subregions.
evidence_reasoning: This is the primary conclusion drawn from the convergence data.

claim: The findings locate a merging of sensory and corollary pathways in specific cerebellar subregions.
source_text: These findings establish the multimodal nature of granule cells and locate a merging of sensory and corollary pathways in specific cerebellar subregions.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the regional mapping and M1 connectivity data.

claim: Granule cells can generate action potentials in response to a single mossy fiber input.
source_text: Granule cells can generate action potentials in response to a single mossy fiber input (Rancz et al., 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This physiological property is supported by citation to prior electrophysiological work.

claim: Inputs of different modalities can potentially substitute for one another to fire a granule cell.
source_text: Therefore, inputs of different modalities can potentially substitute for one another to fire a granule cell.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the known physiology of granule cells and the observed multimodal convergence.

claim: The interchangeability of multimodal inputs suggests a mechanism for converting motor corollary discharges into sensory coordinates.
source_text: This interchangeability suggests a plausible mechanism for converting motor corollary discharges into sensory coordinates, as outlined below.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative mechanistic proposal based on the anatomical findings.

claim: BPN neurons driven by cortical motor commands that do not directly participate in movement generation carry corollary discharges by definition.
source_text: Since these BPN neurons will be driven by cortical motor commands that do not directly participate in movement generation, by definition they can be considered to carry corollary discharges.
evidence_reasoning: This applies the definition of corollary discharge to the observed anatomical pathway.

claim: Corollary discharge-driven predictions will contain some degree of error.
source_text: Corollary discharge-driven predictions will contain some degree of error, which is thought to be computed by comparing pure sensory models against forward models (Mazzoni and Krakauer, 2006; Shadmehr et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established motor control theory supported by citations.

claim: Areas containing granule cells where corollary and sensory information converge might represent components of forward models.
source_text: As described above, areas containing granule cells where corollary and sensory information converge might represent components of forward models.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative functional interpretation of the anatomical findings.

claim: Areas where proprioceptive streams are isolated from corollary/pontine information may represent pure sensory models.
source_text: Other areas where proprioceptive streams are isolated from corollary/pontine information may represent what actually occurred and thus may drive pure sensory models.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative functional interpretation of the regional variation in convergence patterns.

claim: Corollary and sensory information converge in precerebellar neurons of the spinal cord.
source_text: Previously, corollary and sensory information has been shown to converge in the first stage of proprioceptive processing—in the precerebellar neurons of the spinal cord (Hongo and Okada, 1967; Hongo et al., 1967; Hantman and Jessell, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from prior work supported by citations.

claim: The proprioceptive pathway is intersected by corollary discharges at multiple stages.
source_text: The proprioceptive pathway appears to be intersected by corollary discharges at multiple stages.
evidence_reasoning: This combines prior findings with the current data to infer a hierarchical organization.

claim: The findings confirm a key prediction made by David Marr and James Albus about the associative faculty of granule cells.
source_text: Our findings confirm a key prediction made nearly a half a century ago by David Marr and James Albus about the associative faculty of the most abundant neuron type in the mammalian brain.
evidence_reasoning: This connects the experimental findings to theoretical predictions from classical cerebellar theory.

claim: The multimodal capacity of cerebellar granule cells calls for a systematic investigation of the possible mixtures of mossy fiber inputs throughout the cerebellum.
source_text: The multimodal capacity of cerebellar granule cells calls for a systematic investigation of the possible mixtures of mossy fiber inputs throughout the cerebellum.
evidence_reasoning: This is a recommendation for future research based on the current findings.

claim: Slc17a7 exhibits regional selectivity for both the ECN and the BPN.
source_text: First we searched for genes exhibiting regional selectivity for both the ECN and the BPN. Literature and Allen Institute Anatomic Gene Expression Atlas database searches produced candidates fitting this expression profile
evidence_reasoning: This is implicit in the description of the gene selection strategy and confirmed by the subsequent use of Slc17a7-IRES-Cre mice.

claim: A mossy fiber terminal synapses with granule cell dendrites within a glomerulus.
source_text: A mossy fiber terminal synapses with granule cell dendrites within a glomerulus
evidence_reasoning: This is established anatomical knowledge about cerebellar structure, though stated explicitly in the text.

claim: The TCGO transgenic line labels granule cells with mCitrine.
source_text: TCGO transgene expression in a representative section of cerebellum... TCGO mCitrine expression in boxed area... Maximum projection of labeled granule cells in TCGO mice
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the images in Figure 2 showing mCitrine-labeled granule cells in TCGO mice.

claim: Some medial vermis areas harbor proprioceptive pathways that are segregated from BPN inputs at the cellular level.
source_text: Therefore, vermal areas harbor proprioceptive pathways which are segregated from BPN inputs at the cellular level; this segregation would not be evident with traditional neuro-anatomical techniques.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the observation of predominantly E and E+ granule cells in medial vermis regions shown in Figure 3.

claim: The segregation of proprioceptive and BPN pathways in vermal areas would not be evident with traditional neuro-anatomical techniques.
source_text: Therefore, vermal areas harbor proprioceptive pathways which are segregated from BPN inputs at the cellular level; this segregation would not be evident with traditional neuro-anatomical techniques.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the limitations of traditional methods compared to the synaptic-resolution approach used here.

claim: Lateral vermis, simple lobule, copula of the pyramis and Crus1 intermingle all three granule cell types (E, EB, E+).
source_text: Other areas intermingle all three granule cell types, this category includes lateral vermis, simple lobule, copula of the pyramis and Crus1 (Figure 4).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the mapping data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The densities of granule cell types vary along the dorsal-ventral and medial-lateral axes in areas with intermingled cell types.
source_text: The densities of granule cell type varied in these areas along the dorsal-ventral, and medial-lateral axes.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by the density contour maps in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Areas with intermingled granule cell types deliver multiple types of information to overlying Purkinje cells.
source_text: Thus, these areas deliver multiple types of information to the overlying Purkinje cells and the combinations of these types can vary locally.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about information flow based on the observed granule cell connectivity patterns.

claim: Many parallel fiber inputs to Purkinje cells in convergence hotspots carry both ECN and BPN information.
source_text: Consequently, many parallel fiber inputs to Purkinje cells in these areas carry both ECN and BPN information.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about information transmission based on the high proportion of EB granule cells in these regions.

claim: Proprioception signals muscle stretch and tendon tension.
source_text: By signaling muscle stretch and tendon tension, proprioception is particularly well suited to provide input to the brain's sensory model of body position and kinematics (Bosco and Poppele, 2001; Dietz, 2002).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about proprioception supported by citations.

claim: Many behaviors require predicting the likely consequences of a motor plan prior to, or without, movement.
source_text: Proprioceptive and other sensory afferents deliver accurate post-hoc reports of movements, but many behaviors require predicting the likely consequences of a motor plan prior to, or without, movement (Wolpert and Miall, 1996; Bastian, 2006; Shadmehr et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in motor control theory supported by citations.

claim: Forward models use information about intended movements to predict the likely consequences of a voluntary action.
source_text: Forward models have been proposed to use information about intended movements to predict the likely consequences of a voluntary action (Robinson, 1975; Jordan and Rumelhart, 1992; Wolpert and Miall, 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This is established theory in motor control supported by citations.

claim: Forward models require two inputs: sensory inputs that update the state of the model and corollary discharge signals related to intended actions.
source_text: Forward models require two inputs: sensory inputs (peripheral afference) that update the state of the model and corollary discharge signals related to intended actions.
evidence_reasoning: This is established theory about forward models, implicitly supported by the citations on forward models.

claim: Corollary discharges must be converted from motor to sensory coordinates to predict sensory consequences.
source_text: To predict sensory consequences, corollary discharges are thought to mimic self-generated (reafferent) sensory information. To accomplish this mimicry, corollary discharges must be converted from motor to sensory coordinates, but where and how this occurs in the nervous system is largely unknown.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical requirement for forward models, though the location of this conversion is unknown.

claim: Theory and perturbation studies suggest somatic forward models reside in the cerebellum.
source_text: Theory and perturbation studies suggest somatic forward models reside in the cerebellum (Miall et al., 1993, 2007; Miall, 1998; Wolpert et al., 1998; Blakemore et al., 2000; Pasalar et al., 2006; Ebner and Pasalar, 2008; Ito, 2008; Lesage et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to theoretical and experimental work.

claim: Unimodal granule cells supply segregated input channels to Purkinje cells.
source_text: Unimodal granule cells supply segregated input channels to Purkinje cells, allowing the molecular layer to independently adjust the weights of each modality.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about information processing based on the observed anatomy and knowledge of cerebellar circuitry.

claim: Multimodal granule cells enable Purkinje cells to perform more complex learning operations.
source_text: Prefabricating simple associations in granule cells may enable Purkinje cells to perform more complex learning operations, analogous to the enhanced learning capacity of a multilayer perceptron over a single layer perceptron (Minsky and Papert, 1969).
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative functional interpretation drawing an analogy to computational learning theory.

claim: Multimodal claw-footed granule cells have been observed in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish.
source_text: Multimodal claw-footed granule cells have also been observed in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish, suggesting multimodality is a feature of this morphological cell type that is conserved across vertebrate species and across brain regions (Sawtell, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from prior work supported by citation.

claim: Multimodality is a feature of claw-footed granule cells conserved across vertebrate species and brain regions.
source_text: Multimodal claw-footed granule cells have also been observed in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish, suggesting multimodality is a feature of this morphological cell type that is conserved across vertebrate species and across brain regions (Sawtell, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about evolutionary conservation based on observations in fish and mammals.

claim: The labeling strategy rarely accounted for all presynaptic partners of an individual granule cell.
source_text: The observation that our labeling strategy rarely accounted for all presynaptic partners of an individual granule cell suggests that multimodality is likely a more prevalent feature of cerebellar granule cells than indicated by the convergence of the ECN and BPN pathways reported here.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the observation that many granule cells had unlabeled inputs, leading to the inference that multimodality is underestimated.

claim: Multimodality is likely a more prevalent feature of cerebellar granule cells than indicated by ECN and BPN convergence alone.
source_text: The observation that our labeling strategy rarely accounted for all presynaptic partners of an individual granule cell suggests that multimodality is likely a more prevalent feature of cerebellar granule cells than indicated by the convergence of the ECN and BPN pathways reported here.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the incomplete labeling of inputs.

claim: The associative capacity of the cerebellum largely depends on Purkinje cell plasticity.
source_text: The associative capacity of the cerebellum is thought to largely depend on Purkinje cell plasticity, allowing temporal relationships among inputs to alter the strengths of postsynaptic responses (Marr, 1969; Albus, 1971; Boyden et al., 2004; Gao et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is established theory about cerebellar learning supported by citations.

claim: Motor control systems require knowledge of the environment, body position, and how the body moves to perform skilled behaviors.
source_text: In order to perform skilled behaviors, motor control systems require knowledge of the environment, the position of the body, and how it moves.
evidence_reasoning: This is general knowledge about motor control requirements.

claim: Pontine corollary discharges will stimulate multimodal granule cells and generate parallel fiber output to Purkinje cells.
source_text: Pontine corollary discharges will stimulate these granule cells, generate parallel fiber output to Purkinje cells, and may be processed similar to proprioceptive signals that synapse on the same granule cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative proposal about information processing based on the observed connectivity.

claim: Hijacking the proprioceptive pathway could convert corollary messages from motor to sensory coordinates.
source_text: Although speculative, hijacking this pathway could effectively convert the corollary message from motor to sensory coordinates, and thus in the appropriate reference frame to produce proprioceptive predictions.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as speculative reasoning about a potential mechanism.

claim: Error in corollary discharge-driven predictions is computed by comparing pure sensory models against forward models.
source_text: Corollary discharge-driven predictions will contain some degree of error, which is thought to be computed by comparing pure sensory models against forward models (Mazzoni and Krakauer, 2006; Shadmehr et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is established theory in motor control supported by citations.

claim: Common downstream targets of forward and sensory models may represent loci where error signals are generated.
source_text: Common downstream targets of these identified forward and sensory models may represent loci where intended and actual actions are compared and thus where error signals are generated.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative proposal about error computation based on the observed anatomical organization.

claim: Motor inputs at each level of the proprioceptive pathway will produce unique transformations of sensory streams.
source_text: Neurons of each of these stages are distinguished by their inputs and intrinsic properties. Therefore, motor inputs at each level will produce unique transformations of the sensory streams and thus potentially embody nodes within a hierarchical motor-informed sensory processing system.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about hierarchical processing based on the multi-stage convergence of motor and sensory information.

claim: The proprioceptive pathway potentially embodies nodes within a hierarchical motor-informed sensory processing system.
source_text: Neurons of each of these stages are distinguished by their inputs and intrinsic properties. Therefore, motor inputs at each level will produce unique transformations of the sensory streams and thus potentially embody nodes within a hierarchical motor-informed sensory processing system.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative proposal about hierarchical organization based on the observed multi-stage convergence.
